render.php gates the surface-treatment wrapper on 'fx', which is REGISTERED AT RUNTIME by src/blocks/extensions/fx.js for every qualifying block, not declared in any block.json. The read is LIVE, not dead: PHP does not drop undeclared attrs (only the editor/JS surface does), and the effect is verified working on canary page 2900. Declaring it was tried and reverted - no other block declares 'fx' (before-after/image-sequence declare only fx-family attrs they OWN and control in their own edit.js), so declaring made decorative-image the sole outlier and additionally tripped inspector-scan rule 21, whose SYSTEM_ATTR_RE already excludes extension-injected attrs by design but matches on the name shape ^sgs[A-Z_] and so misses the fx family. Accepted as an extension-ownership gap in this gate, not as dead code.

FALSE POSITIVE — the attr is live at BOTH ends, but neither end contains its literal name. Control: product-card/edit.js mounts <TypographyControls prefix="title" showFontFamily />, and TypographyControls.js:160 builds k.fontFamily = typographyAttrName(prefix, "FontFamily"), reading it at :536 and writing it at :538. Render: helpers-typography.php builds $k_family = sgs_typography_attr($prefix, "FontFamily") and emits font-family when set. This is the documented dynamic-key blind spot — the same one recorded for sgs/before-after tier keys, where the checker cannot follow a key whose tail is a second variable. It surfaced on 2026-08-26 because G4 moved font-family onto the shared helper and deleted the block-private emission that had been the only literal occurrence. VERIFY BEFORE TRUSTING THIS ROW: if TypographyControls stops mounting with showFontFamily on this block, or the helper loses its font-family branch, the attr really is dead and this entry must go.

NOT a false positive — genuinely unread by editor/render (Wave 6/7 media-atom migration, 2026-09-02, D915). block.json's own _comment_sourceAtomPair says so explicitly: this attribute is KEPT DECLARED on purpose, despite being equally dead on the render/editor side as the splitVideo*/splitSvg* siblings that WERE deleted, because scripts/dbschema/check_value_identity.py proved the literal name splitImage is load-bearing for the CLONING PIPELINE's scalar-media role assignment (scripts/data/scalar-media-roles.json, run_mechanism_b branch A) — a real named historical incident (a hero clone put the mobile crop in the desktop attribute when this role mapping was lost). Deleting the declaration would silently break a future hero clone's desktop/mobile image assignment, an out-of-scope subsystem this migration deliberately did not touch. See .claude/decisions.md D915 and .claude/plans/2026-08-30-media-element-architecture-v2.md §17 hero entry.
